title: Cisco Secure Network Analytics Alarm Promotion Health
exclusions: Checks that promotion is writing notable-ready events. It does not judge whether the chosen severities are the right ones.
evidence: Daily alarm and promoted counts, and the days marked not promoting.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Turn on Promote SNA Alarms to ES Notables for All severities, raise a test alarm, and confirm a cisco:sna:notable event appears and status stays ok.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Turn promotion off while alarms keep arriving. The next day with alarms and zero promoted events is marked not promoting.

dataSources: `index=cisco_sna` from the Cisco Security Cloud (7404) SNA input: `sourcetype=cisco:sna` for alarms, and `sourcetype=cisco:sna:notable` when Promote SNA Alarms to ES Notables is enabled. The user guide lists the severities you can promote: All, Critical, Major, Minor, Trivial, or Info. Enterprise Security is required for those events to become findings.
app: Cisco Security Cloud (`CiscoSecurityCloud`, [Splunkbase 7404](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/7404)), Secure Network Analytics input. Splunk Enterprise Security for the findings.
spl:
index=cisco_sna (sourcetype="cisco:sna" OR sourcetype="cisco:sna:notable") earliest=-7d@d latest=@h
| bin _time span=1d
| stats count(eval(sourcetype="cisco:sna")) as alarms count(eval(sourcetype="cisco:sna:notable")) as promoted by _time
| eval promoted_pct=if(alarms > 0, round(100 * promoted / alarms, 1), null())
| eval status=case(alarms > 0 AND promoted = 0, "not promoting", true(), "ok")
| sort - _time
description: Compares daily Cisco SNA alarms with the notable-ready copies the input writes when promotion is on, and marks a day not promoting when alarms arrived and no notable-ready event did.
value: The SOC agreed to handle SNA alarms in Enterprise Security. If promotion is off, or Enterprise Security is not installed, those alarms stay in the SNA index and never reach the queue. This report shows that gap by day.
implementation: Enable Promote SNA Alarms to ES Notables on the SNA input and choose the severities. Run this report daily and alert on status=not promoting.
visualization: Column chart of alarms and promoted by day, and a table of days where status is not promoting.

references.title: Cisco Security Cloud App for Splunk User Guide

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Severity filter** — promoting only Critical while most alarms are Minor makes promoted much smaller than alarms. That is still status ok, because promoted is not zero.

2. **No Enterprise Security** — the user guide says events then do not appear via notable macros. This search counts the notable sourcetype in the index, which can still be written.

**Suppression:** alert when status is not promoting.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Cisco Security Cloud (`CiscoSecurityCloud`, Splunkbase 7404) on the search heads and on the heavy forwarder or Splunk Cloud Inputs Data Manager that runs its modular inputs.
• Splunk Enterprise Security on the search head if promoted alarms should become findings.
• An index for this data (this page uses `cisco_sna`) and a role with `srchIndexesAllowed` on it for the SOC.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
• In Cisco Security Cloud open Application Setup, choose the Secure Network Analytics card, and create an input. Set the index to `cisco_sna`.
• The input writes `cisco:sna` for alarms and `cisco:sna:notable` when promotion is enabled.
• Confirm events arrive: `index=cisco_sna sourcetype="cisco:sna" or sourcetype="cisco:sna:notable" | stats count`.

Step 2 — Create the search
```spl
index=cisco_sna (sourcetype="cisco:sna" OR sourcetype="cisco:sna:notable") earliest=-7d@d latest=@h
| bin _time span=1d
| stats count(eval(sourcetype="cisco:sna")) as alarms count(eval(sourcetype="cisco:sna:notable")) as promoted by _time
| eval promoted_pct=if(alarms > 0, round(100 * promoted / alarms, 1), null())
| eval status=case(alarms > 0 AND promoted = 0, "not promoting", true(), "ok")
| sort - _time
```

Understanding this SPL
• `promoted` counts the notable sourcetype. A day with alarms and zero of those is not promoting.
• The ratio is informational. A severity filter makes it small without meaning promotion is broken.

Step 3 — Validate
• On the SNA input, confirm Promote SNA Alarms to ES Notables is enabled and note which severities are selected. Compare a day of Critical alarms in the console with cisco:sna:notable events.

• Confirm in the vendor console that the same hour shows the same kind of event before trusting a zero or a spike.

Step 4 — Operationalize
• Put the panel on the SOC dashboard for Secure Network Analytics and refresh it hourly.
• Alert when the count drops to zero during a staffed period, which means the input stopped, and throttle for 4 hours.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• status=not promoting and the checkbox is on: Enterprise Security is not on this search head, which the user guide says keeps events out of the notable macros. Install it or accept that findings will not appear.
• Both counts are zero: the input itself is down. See the alarm volume search.
• No data for this sourcetype, with an input error in the Cisco Security Cloud log, means the credential or token is incorrect.
grandmaExplanation: We check that the network alarms Cisco raises are still being copied into the security queue, and we flag days when that copy stopped.
